q1: SELECT beer.name, min_price, bar FROM beer LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS min_price FROM serves GROUP BY beer) AS t ON beer.name = t.beer LEFT OUTER JOIN serves ON beer.name = serves.beer AND min_price = serves.price
q2: SELECT s1.beer, COALESCE(CAST(s1.price AS TEXT), 'None'), COALESCE(s1.bar, 'None') FROM beer AS allb LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT s.beer, MIN(s.price) AS lowest FROM serves AS s GROUP BY beer) AS low ON allb.name = low.beer LEFT OUTER JOIN serves AS s1 ON low.beer = s1.beer

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because they join the 'serves' table differently, which affects the results when there are multiple rows with the same beer and price in the 'serves' table.
counterexample_dsp: The difference arises when a beer is served at the same price by multiple bars. Q1 will return the first bar it encounters for that beer and price, while Q2 will return all bars for that beer and price.
